changes.quote: J.D. Power/National Automobile Dealers Association (NADA) – trade-in or wholesale value: All other states use NADA as their primary collateral value source.
changes.note: Wells Fargo had no valuation rows anywhere in the record — only an ineligible-makes list. Texas books on J.D. Power/NADA trade-in or wholesale; KBB applies in 10 named states. The rebate rule is the sharp one: new vehicle value is invoice or book MINUS any manufacturer rebate above $5,000, so a big rebate cuts the collateral value the advance is calculated on. Also the full alternate-valuation ladder for when the book has no number, which ends at 50% of invoice on older units.

changes.note: Small but absent: the 12-month floor, and the warning that re-structuring a funded-shape deal can move the decision, stips, rate or term rather than just the payment.

ambiguities.note: The 6-row x 4-mileage-band term matrix matches the sheet cell for cell — 84 months only under 45,000 miles on units up to 3 years old, down to 51 months everywhere past 120,000. So do the 135% LTV, the 84-month restriction (120%, PTI 15%, Tiers 1-2, no thin file or first-time buyers), the $5,000.01 / $7,500.01 minimums at the 63-month line, and the $5,000 compensation cap.

18 pages rendered; this proposal draws on pages 2 and 9. Pages 3-8 and 10-18 cover the aftermarket product matrix, funding checklist, POR/POI documents, additional programs, excluded collateral and the Dealer Desk — material the record's backend, id and income sections already cover in detail. The backend matrix in particular (total $6,000 or 20% to $12,500, VSC, GAP with its state LTV floors, tire & wheel, maintenance, windshield) is unusually complete. Say the word if you want those pages verified line by line.
